SMTO-POL-0017 — The Agent's code or task list wasn't in the required layout

GUID: 987be870-f786-4a5e-8b32-e491f88cb2e5
Slug: strict-schema-guard
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent wrote a small Python program or a task checklist that isn't laid out the way SMTO requires, for example a checklist with more than 64 items. SMTO refused it before running anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment to see whether the Agent rewrites the code or checklist and carries on by itself. SMTO tells the Agent exactly which layout rule was broken, so it can fix the step.
  2. If the task stops, reply asking the Agent to continue and to group large jobs into 64 checklist items or fewer. A task checklist can hold at most 64 items, so long lists must be grouped.
  3. If you gave SMTO the Python code yourself, put all of it, including imports, inside one function named main(inputs) (or transform(inputs) for data changes). SMTO calls that function itself and refuses code that runs anything outside it.

What success looks like

  • The step runs, or the checklist updates, without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Agent Checks to get past this; badly laid-out code or lists could then run unpredictably.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Python action or transform failed the strict entry-point rules (code must start with def main(inputs) or def transform(inputs), with no decorators, annotations, defaults or top-level statements), or a task-board update exceeded the 64-outcome limit.

What this means

  • Python entrypoint/schema rules or the task board's 64-outcome bound were violated before the requested representation could be accepted. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Python entrypoint/schema rules or the task board's 64-outcome bound were violated before the requested representation could be accepted.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the failure branch: Python entry function/signature and top-level statements, or the task-board item count; these require different corrections.

How to fix it

  • Read the message to see which rule failed (execution/python.py validate_python and _assess_python_schema; native/task_board.py). Put all imports and statements inside the single undecorated def main(inputs) or def transform(inputs) entry function, or reduce the task board to at most 64 outcomes; keep schema.strict_validation enabled.
  • Correct the named field or narrow the task board to its supported bound. Keep strict schema validation enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Python passes its entrypoint/schema check or the board fits its supported count, as appropriate to the failed operation.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the guard as a routine remedy.
  • Do not substitute a different timeout, permission or model setting for this control.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
